title: The State of Knowledge of Soil Biodiversity
text: Soil biodiversity supports nutrient cycling, plant growth, soil productivity, water filtration, carbon sequestration and environmental protection. Sustainable soil management can help prevent soil biodiversity loss.

title: Soil organic carbon
text: Soil organic carbon is a key indicator of soil health. Soil organic matter stores and releases water and nutrients necessary for plant growth and contributes to soil ecosystem services and resilience.

title: Agroforestry
text: Agroforestry integrates trees with crops or livestock. It can strengthen soil fertility, water regulation, biodiversity and resilience. Local conditions and species selection matter.

title: Agroforestry boosts soil health in the humid and sub-humid tropics: A meta-analysis
text: A meta-analysis reported lower erosion, higher infiltration and increased soil organic carbon under agroforestry compared with crop monocultures in the humid and sub-humid tropics. Effects are context dependent.

title: Soil organic cover
text: Keeping soil covered with residues or cover crops can protect soil, recycle nutrients, improve structure and promote biodiversity in agro-ecosystems. Cover crops can be useful in semi-arid or degraded areas.

title: 5 science-backed solutions for a climate-resilient future
text: FAO describes agroforestry as a climate-resilient practice that can help with drought and flood resilience, soil health, carbon sequestration and biodiversity. Benefits vary by site and design.
